 South Africa leave Bangladesh reeling heading into final day
 Bangladesh trail by 57 runs with half the side gone in the first Test in Johannesburg with a day’s play left.
 18 November, 2026 MATCH CENTRE 
 South Africa strengthened their position in the ICC World Test Championship 2025–27 contest against Bangladesh, building a 157-run first-innings lead before reducing the visitors to 100/5 in their second innings.
 View this post on Instagram 
 South Africa resumed Day 4 at 386/7 after persistent rain on Day 3 washed out the final two sessions of play.
 Ryan Rickelton continued his composed knock to bring up his fourth Test century before Litton Das brought his innings to an end with a stumping. 
 The Bangladesh wicket-keeper also etched his name in the record books, registering the most dismissals by a wicket-keeper in a single Test innings .
 View this post on Instagram 
 Kagiso Rabada provided valuable runs down the order, producing a career-best Test score of 72 before being dismissed. 
 Dane Paterson chipped in with 29, while Temba Bavuma, who had retired out on Day 3, returned to the crease to remain unbeaten on 69.
 South Africa were eventually bowled out for 557, securing a commanding first-innings lead of 157 runs.
 View this post on Instagram 
 Trailing by 157 runs, Bangladesh endured a disastrous start to their second innings, losing Tanzid Hasan and Mominul Haque for single-digit scores to Marco Jansen and Kagiso Rabada in the eighth and ninth overs.
 Skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto showed some promise but his stay at the crease was cut short by Simon Harmer, who struck again to dismiss Mahfijul Islam and prevent Bangladesh from building any momentum.
 Rabada returned to the attack to remove Towhid Hridoy, who had scored a century in the first innings, leaving Bangladesh reeling at 100/5.
 Bad light brought an early end to proceedings, with Bangladesh still trailing by 57 runs.
